profile.address: 17, Cable Drive, Bayview, Tuckerton, Ocean County, New Jersey, 08087
profile.reading: This facility is Tuckerton, New Jersey's cable landing station for the decommissioned TAT-14 transatlantic fiber-optic cable system, an underground installation built atop infrastructure originally constructed to Cold War specifications for the earlier, also-decommissioned TAT-3, TAT-4, and TAT-8 systems. TAT-14 itself was a ring-topology system connecting six landing points (Tuckerton/Manasquan, New Jersey on the US side, plus Blaabjerg, Denmark; Norden, Germany; Katwijk, Netherlands; Saint-Valery-en-Caux, France; and Widemouth Bay, UK), spanning roughly 15,428 kilometers with a total design capacity of 9.38 Tbit/s using wavelength-division multiplexing. It became operational March 21, 2001, was owned by a consortium of roughly 30 telecommunications operators including AT&T, BT Group, Deutsche Telekom, Vodafone, Verizon, and Sprint among others, and ceased use on December 15, 2020, with permanent physical dismantling beginning in 2021. Tuckerton's cable landing infrastructure remains active today through a separate, currently operating cable, GlobeNet, tracked elsewhere in this registry under its own GlobeNet operator record. Because TAT-14 itself is fully decommissioned and dismantled, this entry does not assert a current operational role for AT&T at this specific address, nor a current square footage or capacity figure; AT&T's historical role here was as one of roughly 30 consortium owners of a now-retired cable system rather than sole operator of an active facility.

reading.body:
This entry documents a cable landing station in Tuckerton, New Jersey that is no longer operational for AI infrastructure purposes. TAT-14, the transatlantic fiber-optic cable system that this facility housed, ceased operation on December 15, 2020, and was permanently dismantled beginning in 2021. The facility sits on Cold War-era infrastructure originally built for earlier decommissioned cable systems, TAT-3, TAT-4, and TAT-8, also no longer in service.

AT&T's role here was as one of approximately 30 consortium owners of TAT-14 rather than as a sole operator of an active data center. The published specifications do not provide current square footage, power capacity, or operational status for this address, and research to date has not confirmed any current AT&T operational role at this specific location. A separate cable landing facility, GlobeNet, operates elsewhere in Tuckerton and is tracked under its own operator record.

This facility does not represent available compute capacity for AI training or inference. It should not be ranked among active data center campuses for the purposes of assessing AI infrastructure constraints.
